messages:
incident-bot: Pager created: P1 latency SLO breach on production streaming (p99). Links: https://pager.redwood/INC-2090123456. Alerting oncall-eng-sre.

aj_malhotra: seeing p99 ≈ 4.5s across streaming endpoints, p95 up ~1.8s. Spike started ~5m after deploy of prefix-hash change. Lots of stalled streams (clients seeing pauses mid-token).

kai: which routes are degraded? any regional skew?

sara: metrics snapshot (last 15m):
```
route: /v1/stream/generate
p95: 1800ms
p99: 4500ms
stream-stall-rate: 12% -> baseline 1.6%
cache-hit-rate (prefix-cache): global 18% -> baseline 72%
error-rate: 0.9% (timeouts)
```

eng_lead_maya: rolling change merged in PR #3245 ~00:32 UTC — altered prefix normalization (trim + lowercase + strip-leading-zeros). That changed prefix distribution; QA didn't show issue on staging. Deployed to prod 00:58 UTC.

ops_sam: paging in ops. I'm going to disable prefix-cache routing for realtime routes to force model-local KV path as short-term fallback. Running: `redwoodctl rollout set --service prefix-cache --policy disabled --selector "route:stream"`

oncall-bot: Handoff: oncall_sre has accepted. Please use /handoff when switching.

oncall_sre: taking over. I see strong correlation between deploy and cache miss surge. Prioritizing rollback of the prefix normalization change.

aj_malhotra: quick mitigation steps proposed:
- rollback PR #3245 (deploy prefix-hash:v1)
- if rollback will take >10m, disable prefix-cache for streaming routes (ops_sam already doing)
- warm cache back via synthetic replay of recent prefixes for top tenants

kai: warming script ready: `./tools/warm_prefixes.sh --from recent-logs --top 5000` will replay prefixes at low QPS to the prefix-cache. Usage example: `cat recent-prefixes.txt | xargs -n1 -P10 curl -X POST https://cache.internal/warm -d @-`

customer-ops: customer impact: two enterprise tenants (cust-A, cust-B) reported streaming stalls and increased tail latency starting 01:02 UTC -> support tickets created #T-8842 #T-8843. Some customer requests timed out (client retries visible).

eng_lead_maya: added note: the normalization change removed a compatibility step that previously preserved a small range of uppercase prefixes. That concentrated many keys into fewer cache shards — increased eviction and reduced hit-rate.

ops_sam: rollback started: `deploy revert prefix-normalization --to v1 --wait` — ETA ~6m. Also bumping cache TTLs on prefix-cache to 10m temporarily: `redis-cli -h prefix-redis CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy volatile-lru` and adjust TTLs via config push.

sara: after rollback (00:13 after start):
```
p95: 700ms
p99: 2200ms
stream-stall-rate: 2.1% (nearing baseline)
cache-hit-rate: 65% -> improving
```

aj_malhotra: good progress. Still monitoring - there are residual tail spikes on a handful of hosts likely due to cold shards. Plan: keep prefix-cache disabled for streaming routes for 30m, continue warming top prefixes, and keep canary monitors for p99 < 1.5s.

oncall_sre: agreed. I'll keep the rotation and page escalation open until metrics stable for 30m. Scheduling postmortem with eng-runtime, eng-ml, and customer-ops tomorrow.

customer-ops: customers informed via status page and direct emails for affected tenants; support triage ongoing.

eng_lead_maya: root cause summary (prelim): "prefix normalization change reduced key entropy -> cache concentration -> high eviction -> low hit rate -> increased streaming tail latency and stalls." Fix: revert + rework normalization logic to preserve entropy.

ops_sam: scripts run to warm top-2000 prefixes completed. Synthetic traffic showing hit-rate returning to normal.

sara: final quick check at last minute: p99 1.1s, stream-stall 1.5%, cache-hit-rate 71%.

aj_malhotra: marking incident as mitigated for now. Will run a 72h regression monitor and follow up on release gating for prefix-hash changes (add canary env + perf smoke). :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: Incident mitigation noted. Please add severity and timeline to postmortem doc: https://wiki.redwood/incidents/2090123456-postmortem

aj_malhotra: creating postmortem. Will include timeline, logs, commands, and remediation tracking. Closing thread when postmortem is posted. :thumbsup:
